Data sharing and personalization in certain Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).

Restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps (personal accounts only)

Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)

  • You can only turn on this setting from a web browser.

Smart features in Gmail, Chat & Meet

When you turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, you agree to let Gmail, Chat and Meet use your content and activity in these products to personalize your experience in those apps.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in Gmail, Chat and Meet that include:

  • Automatic email filtering / categorization (Primary/Social/Promotions)
  • Smart Compose (suggested text) in email
  • Smart Reply (suggested quick replies) in email
  • Summary cards above emails (travel, package tracking, and more) The setting controls app-level smart features which personalize your experience within Gmail, Chat, or Meet. Changes to this setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Google Workspace setting.

When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Gmail, Chat, and Meet. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

Even if you turn off smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, some smart features with individual on and off settings are still available. Some examples include:

  • Conversation summaries in Chat
  • Smart Reply in Chat Smart features in Google Workspace

When you turn on smart features in Google Workspace, you agree to let Google Workspace use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience across Workspace. Workspace includes apps for businesses and schools, such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more. To learn more, visit the Workspace website.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences across Workspace that include:

  • Show events from Gmail in Calendar (such as flight itineraries and invitations).
  • Personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results) in products like Drive.
  • Ask Gemini to summarize content, create drafts, and find key information, along with other Google Workspace with Gemini features. When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Google Workspace products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

Changes to the smart features in Google Workspace setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet setting described above.

Smart features in other Google products

When you turn on smart features in other Google products, you agree to let Google use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience in other Google products.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in other Google products that include:

  • Restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps (personal accounts only)
  • Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in Search services (personal accounts only) When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in other Google products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

In addition, data sharing and personalization in other Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).

Even when the setting for smart features in other Google products is turned off, if you choose to share your Workspace data through screen actions (including screenshots), some smart features in other Google products will still be available. An example is when you use screen actions to chat with Gemini Apps.

Learn how smart features use your Google Workspace content & activity

Important: By default, smart feature settings are off if you live in:

  • The European Economic Area
  • Japan
  • Switzerland
  • The United Kingdom When smart features are on, your data may be used to improve these features. Across Google and Workspace, we’ve long shared robust privacy commitments that outline how we protect user data and prioritize privacy. Generative AI doesn’t change these commitments — it actually reaffirms their importance. Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet & Vids protects your data.
Change smart feature settings

Learn how to change your smart feature settings in different Google Workspace products. You can change smart feature settings on your computer or in the Gmail app for Android, iPhone, or iPad.

Change smart feature settings for Gmail, Chat & Meet

Important: Changes to smart feature settings apply across all devices and apps where you’re signed in.

  • If you’re on the mobile Gmail app but don’t get a notification about the changes, update your app.
  • Some changes made on your computer don’t reflect in the mobile app.
  • On your computer, go to Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • In the “General” tab, scroll to “Smart features.”
  • Next to “Turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet,” check or uncheck the box.
Change smart feature settings for Google Workspace & other Google products
Gmail
  • On your computer, go to Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • Under the “General” tab, scroll to “Google Workspace smart features.”
  • Click Manage Workspace smart feature settings.
  • Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  • At the bottom right, click Save.
Google Calendar
  • On your computer, go to Calendar.
  • At the top right, click Settings Settings.
  • Under “General,” click Google Workspace smart features Manage Workspace smart features settings.
  • Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  • At the bottom right, click Save.
Google Chat
  • On your computer, go to Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings Data Privacy.
  • Under “Google Workspace smart features,” click Manage settings.
  • Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  • At the bottom right, click Save.
Google Drive
  • On your computer, go to Drive.
  • At the top right, click Settings Settings.
  • Click Privacy.
  • Click Manage Workspace smart feature settings.
  • Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  • At the bottom right, click Save.
Google Meet
  • On your computer, go to Meet.
  • At the top right, click Settings General.
  • Next to “Google Workspace smart features,” click Manage.
  • Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace

Learn how Google handles data in connection with smart feature settings

If you have a personal Google Account, this notice and our Privacy Policy describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

If you have a work or school Google Account, this notice and the Google Cloud Privacy Notice describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

What are Google’s legal bases of processing for users in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland?

For users based in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland, Google processes your information for the purposes, and on the legal grounds, described below.

When we refer to “your Workspace Content & Activity” below, we mean content from Workspace apps such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more, and related data about how you use Workspace products.

Google’s legal bases are:

  • Your consent. We rely on your consent for Google to use your Workspace Content & Activity, when you turn on any of the smart features settings for Google Workspace, for the following purposes:
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in Gmail, Chat and Meet. For example, when you turn the smart features in Gmail, Chat and Meet setting on, you can get experiences that include Gmail Smart Compose (suggested text in email).
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience across Google Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in Google Workspace setting on, you can get experiences that include personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results). This setting does not affect your control over the smart features setting that personalizes your experience in Gmail, Chat, and Meet.
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in other Google products outside of Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in other Google products setting on, you can get experiences that include restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps. Data sharing and personalization in certain products may be subject to additional controls such Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).
  • You can revoke your consent to any of these purposes at any time by turning off the relevant setting as described in the “Change smart feature settings” section above.
  • Google and third parties’ legitimate interests with appropriate safeguards to protect your privacy.
    • To improve our services. If you have turned on any of the smart features settings, we may also process your Workspace Content & Activity to improve these features.
    • Processing information for this purpose is necessary for the legitimate interests of Google and our users in:
      • Providing, maintaining and improving services for our users (such as a flight confirmation email you receive being used to create a summary card that appears in your Gmail).
      • Developing new products and features that are useful for our customers and users (for example, processing aggregated Gmail data helped us develop and launch Smart Compose suggestions as you enter text in Gmail).
      • Performing research that benefits our users and the public (such as to conduct a user study that helped us develop and launch Smart Reply suggested responses in Gmail).
    • Learn more about how we’re protecting your Google Workspace data in the era of generative AI. How long is your Workspace Content & Activity used to provide smart features and to improve these features?

Your Workspace Content & Activity is used to provide you with smart features as long as the relevant smart feature setting is turned on. Turning off a smart feature setting or deleting your Workspace Content & Activity stops that data from being used to provide relevant smart features to you in the future.

Turning off a smart feature setting means your Workspace Content & Activity will no longer be used to improve the relevant smart features moving forward. The learnings developed from this improvement process may persist even after you turn off a smart feature setting or delete your Workspace Content & Activity from your Google Account. However, turning off a smart feature setting means that your Workspace Content & Activity would no longer be actively processed to improve the relevant smart features after you have turned the setting off.

Learn about smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products (Android)

Learn about smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products

To give you more granular control over your data, we’ve updated our smart feature settings for Google Workspace. This update turns the existing control into two distinct settings that govern different product experiences. These updates also give you more choice and control over your data, and do not alter our underlying data handling practices or our robust privacy commitments.

In Calendar, Chat, Drive, Gmail, Meet, and Voice, you can manage smart feature settings. Depending on your smart feature settings, you can do things like:

  • Use Gemini in Google Workspace to reference Drive files from Gmail.
  • Automatically add events such as flights from Gmail to Calendar.
  • Compile loyalty cards and tickets from your inbox into Google Wallet.
  • Track an upcoming order using summary cards in Gmail.
  • Record, transcribe, and summarize notes in Meet and Voice.

Learn about smart feature settings & experiences

Each Workspace smart feature setting works independently from one another and provides different experiences. For example, you can turn on smart features for Google Workspace, and turn off smart features for other Google products. To understand how each smart feature setting works, use the table below.

Smart feature setting

Where to find the setting

Description

Experience example

Controls use of your Workspace data to provide smart features in other Google products.

Data sharing and personalization in certain Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).

Restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps (personal accounts only)

Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)

  • You can only turn on this setting from a web browser.

Smart features in Gmail, Chat & Meet

When you turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, you agree to let Gmail, Chat and Meet use your content and activity in these products to personalize your experience in those apps.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in Gmail, Chat and Meet that include:

  • Automatic email filtering / categorization (Primary/Social/Promotions)
  • Smart Compose (suggested text) in email
  • Smart Reply (suggested quick replies) in email
  • Summary cards above emails (travel, package tracking, and more) The setting controls app-level smart features which personalize your experience within Gmail, Chat, or Meet. Changes to this setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Google Workspace setting.

When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Gmail, Chat, and Meet. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

Even if you turn off smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, some smart features with individual on and off settings are still available. Some examples include:

  • Conversation summaries in Chat
  • Smart Reply in Chat Smart features in Google Workspace

When you turn on smart features in Google Workspace, you agree to let Google Workspace use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience across Workspace. Workspace includes apps for businesses and schools, such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more. To learn more, visit the Workspace website.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences across Workspace that include:

  • Show events from Gmail in Calendar (such as flight itineraries and invitations).
  • Personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results) in products like Drive.
  • Ask Gemini to summarize content, create drafts, and find key information, along with other Google Workspace with Gemini features. When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Google Workspace products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

Changes to the smart features in Google Workspace setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet setting described above.

Smart features in other Google products

When you turn on smart features in other Google products, you agree to let Google use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience in other Google products.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in other Google products that include:

  • Restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps (personal accounts only)
  • Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in Search services (personal accounts only) When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in other Google products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

In addition, data sharing and personalization in other Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).

Even when the setting for smart features in other Google products is turned off, if you choose to share your Workspace data through screen actions (including screenshots), some smart features in other Google products will still be available. An example is when you use screen actions to chat with Gemini Apps.

Learn how smart features use your Google Workspace content & activity

  • The European Economic Area

  • Switzerland
  • The United Kingdom When smart features are on, your data may be used to improve these features. Across Google and Workspace, we’ve long shared robust privacy commitments that outline how we protect user data and prioritize privacy. Generative AI doesn’t change these commitments — it actually reaffirms their importance. Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet & Vids protects your data.
Change smart feature settings

Learn how to change your smart feature settings in different Google Workspace products. You can change smart feature settings on your computer or in the Gmail app for Android, iPhone, or iPad.

Change smart feature settings for Gmail, Chat & Meet

Important: Changes to smart feature settings apply across all devices and apps where you’re signed in.

  • If you’re on the mobile Gmail app but don’t get a notification about the changes, update your app.
  • Some changes made on your computer don’t reflect in the mobile app.
  • On your Android phone or tablet, open Gmail .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings.
  • Select the account you want to change.
  • Scroll to the “General” section.
  • Next to “Smart features,” check or uncheck the box.
Change smart feature settings for Google Workspace & other Google products
  • On your Android phone or tablet, open Gmail .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings.
  • Select the account you want to change.
  • Under “General,” tap Google Workspace smart features.
  • To turn smart features on or off, tap the box next to:
    • “Smart features in Google Workspace”
    • “Smart features in other Google products”

When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Google Workspace products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

Changes to the smart features in Google Workspace setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet setting described above.

Smart features in other Google products

When you turn on smart features in other Google products, you agree to let Google use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience in other Google products.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in other Google products that include:

  • Restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps (personal accounts only)
  • Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in Search services (personal accounts only) When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in other Google products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

In addition, data sharing and personalization in other Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).

Even when the setting for smart features in other Google products is turned off, if you choose to share your Workspace data through screen actions (including screenshots), some smart features in other Google products will still be available. An example is when you use screen actions to chat with Gemini Apps.

Change smart feature settings

Learn how to change your smart feature settings in different Google Workspace products. You can change smart feature settings on your computer or in the Gmail app for Android, iPhone, or iPad.

Change smart feature settings for Gmail, Chat & Meet

Important: Changes to smart feature settings apply across all devices and apps where you’re signed in.

  • If you’re on the mobile Gmail app but don’t get a notification about the changes, update your app.
  • Some changes made on your computer don’t reflect in the mobile app.
  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Gmail app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings.
  • Under “General,” tap Data privacy.
  • Turn Smart features on or off.
Change smart feature settings for Google Workspace & other Google products
  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Gmail app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings.
  • Under “General,” tap Data privacy.
  • Tap Google Workspace smart features.
  • Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  • At the top right, tap Done.
Learn how Google handles data in connection with smart feature settings

If you have a personal Google Account, this notice and our Privacy Policy describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

If you have a work or school Google Account, this notice and the Google Cloud Privacy Notice describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

What are Google’s legal bases of processing for users in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland?

For users based in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland, Google processes your information for the purposes, and on the legal grounds, described below.

When we refer to “your Workspace Content & Activity” below, we mean content from Workspace apps such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more, and related data about how you use Workspace products.

Google’s legal bases are:

  • Your consent. We rely on your consent for Google to use your Workspace Content & Activity, when you turn on any of the smart features settings for Google Workspace, for the following purposes:
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in Gmail, Chat and Meet. For example, when you turn the smart features in Gmail, Chat and Meet setting on, you can get experiences that include Gmail Smart Compose (suggested text in email).
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience across Google Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in Google Workspace setting on, you can get experiences that include personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results). This setting does not affect your control over the smart features setting that personalizes your experience in Gmail, Chat, and Meet.
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in other Google products outside of Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in other Google products setting on, you can get experiences that include restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps. Data sharing and personalization in certain products may be subject to additional controls such Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).
  • You can revoke your consent to any of these purposes at any time by turning off the relevant setting as described in the “Change smart feature settings” section above.
  • Google and third parties’ legitimate interests with appropriate safeguards to protect your privacy.
    • To improve our services. If you have turned on any of the smart features settings, we may also process your Workspace Content & Activity to improve these features.
    • Processing information for this purpose is necessary for the legitimate interests of Google and our users in:
      • Providing, maintaining and improving services for our users (such as a flight confirmation email you receive being used to create a summary card that appears in your Gmail).
      • Developing new products and features that are useful for our customers and users (for example, processing aggregated Gmail data helped us develop and launch Smart Compose suggestions as you enter text in Gmail).
      • Performing research that benefits our users and the public (such as to conduct a user study that helped us develop and launch Smart Reply suggested responses in Gmail).
    • Learn more about how we’re protecting your Google Workspace data in the era of generative AI. How long is your Workspace Content & Activity used to provide smart features and to improve these features?

Your Workspace Content & Activity is used to provide you with smart features as long as the relevant smart feature setting is turned on. Turning off a smart feature setting or deleting your Workspace Content & Activity stops that data from being used to provide relevant smart features to you in the future.

Turning off a smart feature setting means your Workspace Content & Activity will no longer be used to improve the relevant smart features moving forward. The learnings developed from this improvement process may persist even after you turn off a smart feature setting or delete your Workspace Content & Activity from your Google Account. However, turning off a smart feature setting means that your Workspace Content & Activity would no longer be actively processed to improve the relevant smart features after you have turned the setting off.

Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet & Vids protects your data

Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet & Vids protects your data

Across Google and Workspace, we’ve long shared robust privacy commitments that outline how we protect user data and prioritize privacy. Generative AI doesn’t change these commitments — it actually reaffirms their importance.

Our privacy commitments to all Workspace users

Generative AI does not change our foundational privacy protections for giving users choice and control over their data. To that end, here are key facts about how Workspace data is handled.

  • Your data is your data. The content that you put into Google Workspace services (emails, documents, etc.) is yours. We never sell your data, and you can delete your content or export it.
  • Your data stays in Workspace. We do not use your Workspace data to train or improve the underlying generative AI and large language models that power Gemini, Search, and other systems outside of Workspace without permission.
  • Your privacy is protected. Interactions with intelligent Workspace features, such as accepting or rejecting spelling suggestions, or reporting spam, are anonymized and/or aggregated and may be used to improve or develop helpful Workspace features like spam protection, spell check, and autocomplete. These Workspace features are developed with strict privacy protections that keep users in control.
  • Your content is not used for ads targeting. As a reminder, Google does not collect, scan, or use your content in Google Workspace services for advertising purposes. Important: If you’re a Workspace user with a personal account and you choose to share data, including your Workspace data, with Gemini Apps or Search services for Personal Intelligence, or through screen actions (including screenshots), this data will be processed according to their respective terms and policies, and may be used for model training and improvement. Learn more in the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub or the Search services Frequently Asked Questions.

These are the privacy commitments that Workspace extends to all of its users. But they aren’t just words. To ensure we continually meet these high standards, independent auditors validate our practices against international standards and best practices.

Specific commitments for Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet & Vids

For users with Google AI plans, when using Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet, and Vids, your data is yours and under your control. Whether you ask Gemini to summarize an email or document, write a blog post, or add a unique image to your slide:

  • Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, and Vids uses your content in Google Workspace to provide more useful responses to your prompts and doesn’t use your content to train or improve Gemini or other generative AI models.
  • Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, and Vids doesn’t store your prompt or the generated output without your permission. Note: For users enrolled in the Google Workspace Experiments program, use of Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Vids, and Meet is covered by the Google Workspace Experiments Privacy Notice & Terms for Personal Accounts.

Learn how Gmail blocks your messages

Learn how Gmail blocks your messages

Important: To prevent emails from being blocked or sent to spam, you can find info about spam rates, reputation, and more through Postmaster Tools.

To stop spam, Gmail actively filters emails. Sometimes, we might mark an email as spam and move it to the spam folder. We also try to find ways to reduce the amount of spam sent to Gmail. If we think an email might be spam, we block it.

We only block some emails that look like spam, not all of them. An email might be blocked if it contains words that look like spam or if the sender has a history of sending spam. If you’re an organization or company that sends emails to personal Gmail accounts (@gmail.com or @googlemail.com), review the Email sender guidelines.

If you forward an email to Gmail and your domain also sends spam, learn about best practices for forwarding email to Gmail.

Learn how to navigate around Gmail

Learn how to navigate around Gmail

You can switch between emails, chats, and meetings without the need to open a new tab or window in Gmail.

For this same video with audio descriptions, go to Learn about the new Gmail layout.

When you open Gmail, you can:

  • Open Google Chat and Google Meet from the Gmail main menu.
  • View specific app menus in the collapsible panel.
  • Get notified of new chat messages through notification bubbles.
  • Point to each app’s icon to preview what’s going on.
  • Access other Workspace add-ons like Keep and Tasks from the side panel on the right.
Show or hide Chat or Meet
  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings .
  • In the “Quick settings” menu, under “Apps in Gmail,” click Customize.
  • Next to “Google Chat” or “Google Meet,” click the checkbox.
  • Click Done.
Switch between apps in the main menu

To the left of your inbox, in a collapsible panel, you can switch between Gmail, Chat, or Meet.

  • Switch between apps: Click an app name.
  • Preview an app: Point to an icon.
  • Hide or show the collapsible panel: On the top left, click Show main menu / Hide main menu .
Open apps in the side panel

On the right, in the side panel, you can open other Google apps like Keep or Tasks.

  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • At the bottom right, click Show side panel .
  • On the right, select the product you want to open:
    • Calendar : Check your schedule and add or edit events.
    • Keep : Create a note or list.
    • Tasks : Add to-do items and deadlines.
    • Contacts : Access your contacts.
    • Voice : Make a Google Voice call.
  • To close the app panel, on the right, click Close . Tip: To add more apps to the side panel, click Get add-ons .
Manage Chat notification bubbles

When you get a new message in Chat, the notification appears on the bottom left corner in a bubble. When you point to the bubble, a message preview displays.

Reply to a message in a bubble
  • To open the message and reply directly, click the bubble.
  • To open the message in a pop-up window, click Reply.
Turn notification bubbles on or off

  • At the top right of Gmail, click the status indicator Chat notification settings.

  • In the window that appears, check the boxes next to “Allow Chat notifications” and “Open chat bubbles for new messages.”

  • At the bottom of the window, click Done. Tips:

  • To turn notification bubbles off, uncheck the box next to “Open chat bubbles for new messages.”

  • To open chat bubbles in a pop-up window, uncheck the box “Open chat bubbles in full screen.”

Manage to-dos & topics with AI Inbox

Manage to-dos & topics with AI Inbox

Important: AI Inbox is currently in beta and may change over time. Your use of AI Inbox is covered by the Google Cloud Terms of Service, and the specific terms for pre-release features do not apply.

To help you manage a busy inbox, AI Inbox can show you priority emails and topics.

Learn how AI Inbox works

AI Inbox helps surface to-dos and topics that matter most, all in one place. When you open AI Inbox, there are 2 sections:

  • Suggested to-dos: This section shows high-priority items from incoming emails that need your attention. It also explains what you need to do in bold text, like a due date for a utility or credit-card bill.

  • Topics to catch up on: This section provides a quick summary of important updates across projects and topics. It helps you stay updated on items often scattered in various email threads. Examples include upcoming travel, restaurant reservations, or purchase confirmations. To show the most relevant items, AI Inbox:

  • Only surfaces information from messages in your “Primary” tab and not other tabs, such as “Social” or “Promotions.”

  • Filters out messages like spam or that you archive, delete, mute, or snooze.

  • Does not support attachments, delegated inboxes, or encrypted emails.

What you need

Important: This feature is only available in the US and in English.

  • For personal Google Accounts: You need an eligible Google AI plan:
    • Google AI Plus
    • Google AI Pro
    • Google AI Ultra
  • For work or school accounts: You need a Workspace Enterprise Plus plan with access to Gemini Beta.
    • If you use a work or school account, your admin controls access to Gemini Beta.
    • If you can’t find AI Inbox, your admin may not have Beta features enabled for your organization.
Additional requirement
  • In Gmail, turn on Smart features in Google Workspace and Smart features in other Google products. Learn more about smart features. Tip: After you turn on smart features, it can take a few hours. It may take up to 7 days for your first set of to-dos and topics to appear.
Show or hide AI Inbox
  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • At the top, click Inbox.
  • Next to “Show AI Inbox,” check or uncheck the box.
Open AI Inbox

Important: Your AI Inbox may appear empty if you have not sent or received emails recently.

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • In the left panel, click AI Inbox.

  • To get the latest updates, at the top, click Refresh . Tip: If the information in AI Inbox is outdated:

  • Make sure you have a stable internet connection or Wi-Fi.

  • Confirm that you are in the correct Google Account.

Manage suggested to-dos
  • Take action on an email: Next to a to-do, select an action button, like View or Reply.
  • Open related information: To get more context, click the link next to any item and open the related email, chat, or another source.
  • Complete a to-do: When you finish, click Mark done .
  • Provide feedback or report issues: Next to any item, click More options :
    • Remove to-do: Remove a to-do from your list.
    • Positive feedback or Negative feedback: Rate the quality of a to-do or topic.
    • Report abuse: Report unsafe suggestions to Google.
Review topics to catch up on
  • Open related information: To get more context, click the link next to any item and open the related email, chat, or another source.
  • Mark all emails as read: To acknowledge unread updates in AI Inbox, click Mark all as read. This also changes all affected emails to read in your Gmail inbox.
  • Provide feedback or report issues: Next to any item, click More options :
    • Positive feedback or Negative feedback: Rate the quality of a to-do or topic.
    • Report abuse: Report unsafe suggestions to Google.

Package tracking in Gmail

Package tracking in Gmail

Get a simple and helpful view of your package tracking and delivery information, right in your inbox. Package tracking in Gmail is available for participating carriers in the US.

How package tracking works

If your order email contains a tracking number, Gmail automatically uses the tracking number to look up the order status and make it easy for you to see. Package status will appear in your inbox and at the top of individual emails, showing details like the estimated arrival date and delivery status.

Generally, an order or shipment will be displayed when the confirmation email includes the following information:

  • Tracking number
  • Merchant name and logo
  • Product name and product image
  • Order number
  • Order URL
  • Estimated delivery date Gmail will help keep track of packages across most shopping platforms and shipping carriers for users who have turned on the feature.
Turn package tracking on or off in Gmail

Important: To use package tracking, turn on smart features in your Gmail settings. Learn more about smart features and controls for Google Workspace and other Google products.

To turn package tracking on or off:

  • On your computer, go to Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • In the “General” tab, scroll to the “Package tracking” section.
  • Select the Turn on package tracking box.
  • At the bottom of the page, click Save Changes.
What information is used

If you choose to use packing tracking, your tracking numbers will be identified through automatic processing, similar to what Gmail uses to fight spam and phishing. When a tracking number is identified, Gmail will use it to look up order statuses and surface them in your inbox. Only the tracking number is shared with carrier partners.

To turn package tracking on or off:

  • On your Android phone or tablet, open the Gmail app .
  • Tap Menu Settings the account you want to change.
  • Scroll to the “General” section.
  • Next to “Package tracking,” check or uncheck the box.
What information is used

If you choose to use packing tracking, your tracking numbers will be identified through automatic processing, similar to what Gmail uses to fight spam and phishing. When a tracking number is identified, Gmail will use it to look up order statuses and surface them in your inbox. Only the tracking number is shared with carrier partners.

Package tracking in Gmail (Computer)

Package tracking in Gmail

Get a simple and helpful view of your package tracking and delivery information, right in your inbox. Package tracking in Gmail is available for participating carriers in the US.

How package tracking works

If your order email contains a tracking number, Gmail automatically uses the tracking number to look up the order status and make it easy for you to see. Package status will appear in your inbox and at the top of individual emails, showing details like the estimated arrival date and delivery status.

Generally, an order or shipment will be displayed when the confirmation email includes the following information:

  • Tracking number
  • Merchant name and logo
  • Product name and product image
  • Order number
  • Order URL
  • Estimated delivery date Gmail will help keep track of packages across most shopping platforms and shipping carriers for users who have turned on the feature.

Proofread your drafts with Gemini in Gmail

Proofread your drafts with Gemini in Gmail

To improve your drafts, you can use Gemini in Gmail to proofread and get advanced grammar, tone, and style suggestions.

What you need
  • For personal Google Accounts: You need one of the following:
    • An eligible Google AI plan:
      • Google AI Plus
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra
    • Access to Google Workspace Experiments.
  • For work or school accounts: You need an eligible Google Workspace plan. Learn more about Gemini features and plans.
Additional requirements
  • For the Gmail app on Android, iPhone, and iPad, Proofread is available in early access.
    • For personal Google Accounts: Access to Google Workspace Experiments is required.
    • For work or school accounts: An eligible Google Workspace plan with access to Gemini Beta is required.
      • If you use a work or school account, your administrator controls access to Gemini Beta.
      • If you can’t find Proofread, your administrator may not have Beta features enabled for your organization.
  • You can proofread your drafts in English globally. If you are in Google Workspace Experiments or Gemini Beta, you also get early access to proofread drafts on the web in:
    • German
    • Japanese
    • Spanish
Accept suggestions in a draft

  • In your draft, click an underlined word or phrase to open the suggestion card.

  • Review the change:

    • To use the suggestion, click it.
    • To dismiss the suggestion, click Ignore .

  • Optional: To give feedback on a suggestion, click Report an issue . Tips:

  • When you ignore a suggestion, it doesn’t reappear for the same word or phrase unless you change the text.

  • To undo a change:

    • On Windows: Press Ctrl + Z.
    • On Mac: Press Cmd + Z.
    • On screen readers:
      • To find underlined words, use your arrow keys.
      • Select Tab Enter.
Turn off Proofread

Important: When you turn off “Proofread,” you won’t get grammar suggestions.

  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • At the top, click General.
  • Next to “Grammar,” click Grammar suggestions off.
Learn about Gemini feature suggestions
  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.
  • Don’t rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial or other professional advice.
  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information.

Report abuse in Gemini in Workspace apps

Report abuse in Gemini in Workspace apps

Important: This article only applies for reporting abuse about Gemini responses. For general feedback about Gemini responses, use Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . The terms in the feedback flow will apply when you submit general feedback.

If you get inaccurate or unsafe responses in Gemini in Workspace apps, you have the option to report them to us. Your feedback helps make Gemini in Workspace apps more helpful, accurate, and safe.

When you report a response, such as spam, fraud, or illegal content, your conversation with Gemini is added to your report, including:

  • Prompts

  • Context documents, emails, and other content

  • The response from Gemini To report abuse in Gemini in a Workspace app:

  • Next to a response, select the Report abuse option.

    • If you can’t find Report abuse, select More options .

  • Select the reason you wish to report content.

  • Click Report. Tip: You can also report a legal issue here.

Send an automatic reply when you’re out of office

Send an automatic reply when you’re out of office

To let others know when you’re out of office or on vacation, you can create a vacation responder in Gmail. When someone sends you a message, they receive an automatic reply.

Set up a vacation responder

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • Under the “General” tab, go to the “Vacation responder” section.

  • Select Vacation responder on.

  • Fill in the date range, subject, and message.

  • Optional: To send the reply to your contacts only, under the message, check the box.

  • At the bottom of the page, click Save Changes. Tips:

  • If you have a signature, it shows below the reply.

  • When your vacation responder is on, a banner shows across the top of your inbox. To turn it off, click End now.

Learn how an automatic reply works

Your automatic reply starts at 12:00 AM on the start date and ends at 11:59 PM on the end date, unless you end it earlier.

In most cases, your reply is only sent to people the first time they message you.

Someone can get your reply more than once if:

  • The same person contacts you again after four days and your automatic reply is still on.
  • You edit the automatic reply.
    • If someone gets your initial automatic reply, then emails you again after you edit the reply, they get the updated email. Tips:
  • To prevent an automatic reply in a conversation thread, add a subject line to your reply. When you add a subject line, the recipient receives your reply in a separate email.
  • Emails sent to your spam folder or addressed to a mailing list you subscribe to don’t get your reply.

Set up & use Gmail offline

Set up & use Gmail offline

You can use Gmail offline to read, search, and reply to messages without an internet connection. To get started, turn on offline mail in Chrome.

Turn on offline mail

Important: You can only use Gmail offline in a Chrome browser window that isn’t in Incognito mode. Download Google Chrome.

  • On your computer, go to Gmail offline settings.

  • Next to “Enable offline mail,” check the box.

  • Choose your settings, such as how many days of messages you want to sync.

  • Click Save changes. Tip: To make it easy to find your offline inbox in Chrome, bookmark Gmail.

  • On your computer, open Chrome.

  • In Chrome, go to Gmail.

  • On the right, in the address bar, select Bookmark .

Learn what to expect when you use Gmail offline
  • Check storage settings: When offline, Gmail only uses the space available to your browser. It’s a fraction of your computer’s total storage.
    • The storage shown in Gmail offline settings is smaller than your computer’s actual available storage.
  • Open your mail: To use Gmail offline, open Chrome and go to Gmail.
    • Or, you can use your bookmark.
  • Send a message: If you send a message offline, it’s saved in a new “Outbox” folder.
    • If you connect to the internet, the message is sent automatically.
  • Download attachments: You can download attachments to your computer and open them with a local application.
    • You can’t preview attachments.
  • Use multiple accounts: You can only use Gmail offline with the account you were signed in to at setup.
    • To enable another account for offline use, sign in to that account and follow the setup steps above.
Fix issues when you use Gmail offline

Your messages don’t sync

This issue can happen if:

  • You run out of storage space: To fix this issue, change your “Offline” settings in Gmail.
    • On your computer, go to Gmail offline settings.
    • Next to “Sync settings,” you can:
      • Click the Down arrow to sync fewer days of messages.
      • Uncheck Download attachments.
  • You close Chrome: Your messages can only sync if Chrome is open. You get an insufficient offline storage error message

When you enable offline mail, you get this message: “Looks like there is not enough space available for offline mail. This may be caused by insufficient hard drive space or a web browser mode.”

This error can happen if:

  • Your hard drive doesn’t have enough space.
  • You use an Incognito window in Chrome.
  • You use a Guest profile in Chrome.
  • Your Chrome settings are set to clear cookies on exit. To check your settings:
    • On your computer, open Chrome.
    • In your address bar, enter “chrome://settings/content/siteData”.
    • Under “Always delete site data from your device when you close Chrome,” make sure that “mail.google.com” or “*.google.com” doesn’t show.
Turn off offline mail

Important: If you delete cookies, you get signed out of sites that remember you and your saved preferences can be removed. This applies every time a cookie is deleted.

Step 1: Remove your offline data
  • On your computer, open Chrome.
  • At the top right, select More Settings .
  • Select Privacy and security Third-party cookies.
  • Select See all site data and permissions Delete all data.
  • To confirm, select Delete.
Step 2: Turn off offline mail
  • On your computer, go to Gmail offline settings.
  • Next to “Enable offline mail,” uncheck the box.

Set your working hours & location

Set your working hours & location

You can use working hours and availability if your account is through your work or school organization. If you don’t see the working hours or location option, your admin could have turned it off for your organization. Who is my administrator?

Turn on working hours

To let people know you’re unavailable when they try to schedule a meeting with you, turn on working hours. You can only turn on working hours from a computer.

  • On your computer, open Google Calendar.
  • At the top right, click Settings Settings.
  • On the left, under “General,” click Working hours.
    • Tip: If your admin has turned on working location, click Working hours & location. Learn more about your administrator.
  • In the “Working hours” section, click Enable working hours.
  • Select the days you work the times you work.
  • You can split the hours you work based on when you’re available.
    • To add more than one time period to your workday, next to a day of the week, click Add .
    • To remove a time period, click Remove . Tip: When you add work hours, the start time must be before the end time.

Calendar may suggest working hours based on your time zone, the work patterns in your country, and your schedule. You can accept, decline, or edit these suggestions. Learn more about Calendar in different time zones.

Add or edit your working location

Set your default working location

  • On your computer, open Google Calendar.
  • At the top right, click Settings Settings.
  • On the left, under “General,” click Working hours & location.
  • Select the days you work. Working hours are already selected if your calendar shows working hours.
  • Next to each day, enter an existing working location or create a new one. Tip: To change your working location, go to a specific day on your calendar and click the location bar. You can apply the change to that specific day or set it to repeat weekly.
Learn more about your working location:

  • When you share your calendar with someone, they can view your working location.

  • To help coordinate in-office time with others, your administrator may ask you to set your working location. If so, a yellow banner at the top of your calendar will show the request.

  • If you have “Make changes & manage sharing” access to a calendar, you can edit the default working location. Learn more about permission settings for shared calendars. Add your working location

  • On your computer, open Google Calendar.

  • Create an all-day event. Learn how to create an all-day event.

  • In the event window that appears, select Working location.

  • Optional: Adjust the dates that you want to add a working location to.

  • Select a location or create a new one.

  • Click Save. Tip: You can also add a working location when you point below a date on your calendar grid and click the “Add location” bar that appears.

Edit your working location for one day

Important: When your calendar is shared with someone with free or busy visibility, they can view your availability and working location.

    • If you click on the starting location, click Edit working location .

    • Select a location or create a new one.

  • Click Save.

  • Choose a frequency, and then click OK. Edit your working location for a range of days

  • On your computer, open Google Calendar.

  • At the top of the event, click Working location.

  • Choose the time and date you want to add a working location.

  • Optional: Make your working location repeat.

    • Click the day and time.
    • Next to “Does not repeat,” click the Down arrow .

  • Choose a location or add a new one.

  • After you create a working location for part of your day, you can drag it to another date or time.

Show when you’re out of office

When you indicate that you’re out of office, your calendar will automatically decline all meetings during that time.

  • On your computer, open Google Calendar.
  • At the top of your calendar, click the first date you’ll be out of the office.
  • Click Out of office.
  • Select the dates that you’ll be out of the office. You can also specify a time.
  • Optional: To schedule out-of-office events that repeat, below the day and time you select, click the drop down menu next to “Does not repeat” choose a frequency.
  • Optional: Change your decline settings and edit your decline message.
  • Click Save.

If you use Gmail for work or school and show when you’re out of office:

Turn on working hours

    • To add more than one time period to your workday, next to a day of the week, click Add .
    • To remove a time period, click Remove . Tip: When you add work hours, the start time must be before the end time.

Calendar may suggest working hours based on your time zone, the work patterns in your country, and your schedule. You can accept, decline, or edit these suggestions. Learn more about Calendar in different time zones.

Share in Chat from Gmail

Share in Chat from Gmail

Users with a work or school account can quickly share an email in a Chat message to keep the email context and avoid long email threads.

Important:

  • Users with a personal account don’t have access to this feature.
  • To share an email in Chat, you must turn on Chat in Gmail.
Share an email in Chat
  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • Open an email.
  • At the bottom of the email, select Share in chat .
    • Tip: To share a specific email in a multiple-email thread, next to the email, click More Share in chat .
  • To add recipients, you can:
    • Click Add everyone from the email.
    • Search or select from listed suggestions.
  • Optional: To remove a recipient, next to the name or space, click Remove .
  • Click Next.
  • Enter your message.
  • Click Send .
    • The recipient gets a link to the email in Chat.
    • Gmail adds an automated reply to the email thread that links to the Chat message.
Learn why you’re unable to share an email in Chat

You can’t share an email in Chat if:

  • You use a personal account.
  • The admin for your work account turned off Chat.
  • You haven’t turned on Chat within Gmail on your computer.
  • The email is spam, phishing, scheduled, in trash, in drafts, or in confidential mode.
  • You open the email in another email app, like Apple Mail or Microsoft Outlook.
  • The email is encrypted with Client-side encryption. Learn about Gmail Client-side encryption.
  • You try to share an email in Chat to more than 50 recipients or to a Google Group.

  • Reply to a message in Google Chat
  • Edit or delete a message in Google Chat
  • Search for Google Chat messages Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad

Suggest times to meet with Gemini in Gmail

Suggest times to meet with Gemini in Gmail

Important: This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Learn about Gemini features and plans.

To set up meetings with one or more people in Gmail, use the “Help me schedule” feature when you draft a message or reply. Based on you and your guests’ availability, Gemini in Gmail generates a list of times when you’re all available.

Insert suggested times in a Gmail message

  • On your computer, go to Gmail.

  • Create or reply to an email with one or more recipients.

  • At the bottom of your message, click Help me schedule .

    • If you can’t find “Help me schedule,” click More options Help me schedule.

  • Review the list of suggested times.

  • At the bottom of the email, click Send. Tips:

  • A maximum of 20 guests can be added to a single schedule.

  • The guest list isn’t updated if the list of email recipients changes after the card is inserted. You need to re-insert the schedule.

  • Gemini in Gmail proposes 4 slots by default.

Update the suggested times card
  • Hover over Edit in Calendar .
  • Select an option:
    • Meeting duration: Change the length of the meeting.
    • Time range: To search for available meeting times, update the time range.
    • Change to text format: Send your meeting times as text instead of a suggestion card.
    • More options: Insert a booking page from your appointment schedule.
Update suggested times based on guest calendars

You can manually review suggested times based on guest calendars.

  • In the suggested times card, click Edit in Calendar .
  • In the “Share your availability” window, you can:
    • Check availability: You can check the availability of any guest’s calendar that you have access to.
    • Change meeting duration: Change the length of the meeting.
    • Add guest time zone: Include the guest’s time zone.
    • Add or remove guests: On the right, add or remove your guests. Suggestions automatically update based on the new guest list.
    • Review time slots: If calendars are busy, Gemini in Gmail can suggest a mix of times.
      • If the time slots are green, all guests are available to meet.
      • If the time slots are amber, there’s a conflict for one or more guests. If this happens, a banner at the top of the window prompts you to manually select time slots. To make sure the chosen time works for your priority guests, review the calendar grid.
  • At the bottom right, click Propose times.
Book time on someone else’s calendar

If you receive suggested times from someone else, you can book a time slot with them. Once booked, a Calendar event is created and all guests receive an event invitation.

  • In the email, select a suggested time.
  • On the “Book your preferred time” page, you can:
    • Confirm the event time: If there are no conflicts with other guests, click Book time for all guests.
    • Look for different times to meet: If there are conflicts, click View all times on calendar.
      • In the window, select a new time slot.
Learn about Gemini feature suggestions
  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.
  • Don’t rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial or other professional advice.
  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information.
Related resources
  • Learn about scheduling events in Gmail
  • Get started with Google Workspace with Gemini

Supported browsers

Supported browsers

You can use Gmail with popular browsers like Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.

Browsers that are supported by Gmail

Important: Any browser you use needs to have cookies and JavaScript turned on.

Gmail works best in the newest and last prior version of these browsers:

  • Google Chrome.
    • To get the best Gmail experience and security updates, upgrade to the latest version of Chrome.
    • If you have a Chromebook, you might need to update your Chromebook’s operating system.
  • Firefox
  • Safari
  • Microsoft Edge
Visit Gmail on your browser
  • On your computer, go to gmail.com.
  • Sign in to Gmail.
Troubleshoot browser errors

Browser isn’t supported

“This browser is not supported.”

If you use a browser that works with Gmail and get this error message, an extension might be causing the problem. Try turning off your browser extensions.

If you use Chrome, learn how to manage extensions.

JavaScript error

“In order to log in to Gmail, your browser must be set to allow JavaScript to set cookies.”

If you get this message, open your browser’s security settings and add mail.google.com to your trusted sites.

“Oops! Gmail won’t work because JavaScript is disabled in your web browser.”

If you get this message, turn on JavaScript, then refresh the page. Instructions for changing your JavaScript settings vary by browser, so do a search for JavaScript and your browser’s name to find the right help page.

If you use Chrome, learn how to change site settings.

Cookie error

“Your browser’s cookie functionality is turned off. Please turn it on.”

If you get this message, do a search for your browser’s name and cookies to find instructions. If you use Chrome, learn how to enable cookies.

Talk naturally with Gmail Live

Talk naturally with Gmail Live

Important: Gmail Live is currently in beta and may change over time. Your use of Gmail Live is covered by the Google Cloud Terms of Service, and the specific terms for pre-release features do not apply.

With Gmail Live, you can have a conversation with Gemini to manage your inbox more efficiently. In Gmail Live, you can:

  • Get quick answers: Ask questions and receive immediate answers based on your emails.
  • Have a natural conversation: Engage in a back-and-forth dialogue with Gmail Live. For example, you can ask, “What’s my flight’s gate number?” or “What’s going on at my kid’s school this week?”
  • Refine your search: Interrupt Gmail Live to change topics or ask follow-up questions to get more granular responses without starting over.
What you need

Important: This feature is only available in English.

  • For personal Google Accounts:
    • You must have an eligible Google AI plan:
      • Google AI Plus
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra
    • You can also access Gmail Live if your account is enrolled in Google Workspace Experiments, which is a trusted tester program to try new AI features. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace Experiments.
  • For work or school accounts: You need an eligible Google Workspace plan with access to Gemini Beta.
    • If you use a work or school account, your admin controls access to Gemini Beta.
    • If you can’t find Gmail Live, your admin may not have Beta features enabled for your organization.
  • The Gmail mobile app: Available on Android, iPhone, and iPad.
Additional requirements
  • Smart features: In Gmail, turn on Smart features in Google Workspace and Smart features in other Google products. Learn more about smart features.
Talk to Gmail Live

Important: At this time, you can’t change the voice of Gmail Live.

  • On your Android phone or tablet, open the Gmail app .
  • At the top, tap Gmail Live .
    • Tip: If it’s your first time, grant the Gmail app microphone permissions and accept the terms and conditions.
  • Start talking.
    • Or, tap a suggested prompt.
  • To exit Gmail Live, tap End .
Mute Gmail Live

You can mute the chat to turn off your microphone and let Gemini finish speaking. This keeps the session active.

  • To mute: When Gmail Live is active, tap Mute .
  • To resume: Go back to your Gmail Live chat and tap Unmute .
View sources for your answers

To verify where answers came from, Gmail Live provides citations.

  • To open the exact emails used for details: Tap links within Gmail Live’s response.
  • To find all sources that contribute to Gmail Live’s response:
    • At the bottom, tap the Sources card. This shows all cited emails.
    • When you tap an email in the source menu, it opens the email and ends your Gmail Live session.
  • Search results:
    • To exit the Gmail Live session and find emails in a standard search layout:
      • Scroll to the bottom of the source menu.
      • Tap View search page.
Manage conversation history

To help you track your previous conversation, Gmail Live saves transcripts in your conversation history with Gemini in Workspace. You can check and delete your conversation history from a web browser.

Manage your conversation history

Learn how to access and manage your Gemini in Workspace conversation history.

Fix problems with Gmail Live
  • Audio muted:
    • If your device volume is at 0%, a warning appears.
    • To hear Gmail Live, tap Turn volume up or use your device’s volume buttons.
  • Microphone permission:
    • If you previously denied microphone access, the session does not start.
      • Tap Settings on the error screen to open your device settings.
      • Allow microphone access for the Gmail app.
  • Connection interrupted:
    • If your internet connection drops, the session disconnects.
    • Check your network connection and tap Try again.
Related resources
  • Learn about smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products
  • Find & manage your Gemini in Workspace conversation history Android iPhone & iPad

Track your purchases in Gmail

Track your purchases in Gmail

You can easily track all your online purchases with Gmail’s Purchases view. It gathers all your order, shipping, and delivery confirmations in one place, and provides a timeline for upcoming deliveries.

Important: This feature is available for personal Gmail accounts.

Check your orders & deliveries
  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • On the left menu bar, click Purchases.
Learn how your purchases are organized

The “Purchases” view organizes your order information into 2 sections:

  • Arriving soon: This section is at the top and shows cards for orders with an estimated delivery date of today or the future. Orders are chronologically listed by the arrival.
    • For more info, select Track package or More details.
  • Purchases: This section is below the “Arriving soon” cards and shows a list of purchase-related emails in your inbox.
Related resources
  • Package tracking in Gmail
  • Use summary cards in Gmail Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad
