Troubleshoot issues with Gmail signatures

Troubleshoot issues with Gmail signatures

An email signature is text, like your contact information or a favorite quote, at the end of an email message. Signatures are automatically added to the end of Gmail messages, like a footer. You can optionally add an image to your Gmail signature. Learn more about Gmail signatures.

If you’re having problems with your Gmail signature, or with images in your signature, try the solutions in this article.

Common signature issues and solutions
  • Signature doesn’t display correctly
  • Extra characters in my signature
  • Can’t format text in my signature
  • Signature hidden by three dots in sent messages
Issues uploading signature image

If you’re having problems uploading an image to your signature, try these solutions:

  • Clear your browser cache
  • Clear cookies for mail.google.com
  • Allow all cookies for Gmail
  • Change Google Drive sharing permissions for the image
  • Upload the image in a Chrome incognito window
  • Upload the image with a different browser
Signature image not formatted correctly

If you’re having problems formatting your signature image, try these solutions:

  • Delete then re-upload the signature image
  • Use a different upload method
  • Use a signature image in the recommended size
Common Gmail signature issues

Try these steps for general issues displaying and formatting Gmail signatures.

Signature doesn’t display correctly

Sometimes Gmail doesn’t correctly display formatted text in a signature. Try removing the formatting:

  • Open Gmail.
  • In the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • In the Signature section, select your signature.
  • Click Remove formatting . A signature image that’s too large can also cause this issue. For a solution, go to Use a signature image in the recommended size.
Can’t format text in my signature

If you can’t format your signature text, and Plain Text appears above the signature box, turn off plain text mode before editing your signature:

  • Open Gmail.
  • Click Compose.
  • In the bottom right, click More options .
  • Uncheck Plain text mode.
Extra characters in my signature

Some versions of Gmail don’t support formatting options, like bold or italics. Formatted text in these Gmail versions can result in extra characters in your signature. To remove the extra characters, remove the formatting from your signature:

  • Open Gmail.
  • In the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • In the Signature section, highlight your signature.
  • Click Remove formatting .
Signature hidden by three dots in sent messages

If you can’t find your signature in a Gmail message, it might be below the body of the message. Signatures are separated from the message body by two dashes.

To show your signature, scroll to the bottom of a message, then click Show trimmed content .

Issues uploading signature image

If you have problems uploading images, try one or more of the solutions in this section. Image upload issues can include:

  • Image doesn’t upload
  • Image doesn’t show in the signature
  • Image added from Google Drive doesn’t show in the signature
  • The only upload option is by URL Note: The instructions in this section are for Chrome. If you use Safari, Firefox, or another browser, check the browser’s support site for instructions.

Clear your browser cache

When you use a browser, like Chrome, some information from visited websites is stored in the browser’s memory cache. Clearing the cache might fix problems with uploading a signature image:

  • On your computer, open Chrome.
  • At the top right, click More Settings.
  • Click More toolsClear browsing data.
  • At the top, choose a time range. To delete everything, select All time.
  • Check the Cached images and files box.
  • Click Clear data. For detailed information about clearing Chrome’s cache, go to Clear cache & cookies.

Clear cookies for mail.google.com

Cookies are files created by websites you visit. They make your online experience easier by saving information about your web browsing. Clearing cookies might fix problems with uploading signature images:

  • On your computer, open Chrome.
  • At the top right, click More Settings.
  • On the left, click Privacy and security.
  • Click Cookies and other site data.
  • Scroll down and click See all cookies and site data.
  • At the top right, enter mail.google.com in the Search cookies field.
  • Click the Remove all button. For detailed information about clearing Chrome cookies, go to Clear, enable, and manage cookies in Chrome.

Allow all cookies for Gmail

You can block or allow all cookies for specific sites. Allowing all cookies for Gmail might fix problems with uploading signature images:

  • On your computer, open Chrome.
  • At the top right, click More Settings.
  • On the left, click Privacy and security.
  • Scroll down to Customized behaviors.
  • Next to Sites that can always use cookies, click Add.
  • In the Add a site box, enter mail.google.com, then click Add. For detailed information about allowing cookies for certain sites, go to Clear, enable, and manage cookies in Chrome.

Change Google Drive sharing permissions for the image

To use a Google Drive image in your signature, the image sharing settings must be set to public.

Important: If you have a work or school account and can only add images from a URL, you can’t change your Google Drive sharing settings for images. To use a Google Drive image in your signature, ask your administrator to let you share images publicly.

  • Select the image file you want to use in your signature.

  • Click Share or Share Get link.

  • Under Get Link, select Change to anyone with the link.

  • To let anyone view your signature image, select Viewer.

  • Click Done. Tips:

  • To add a Drive image to your signature, we recommend the “My Drive” option. Find the image in Drive. Then click Select.

  • If the image file or a Google Doc in Drive with the image is deleted, the image won’t show in the signature. For detailed information about Drive sharing, go to Share files from Google Drive.

Upload the image in a Chrome incognito window

Chrome incognito mode runs in a separate window from the standard Chrome windows. Incognito mode lets you browse the web privately. If you’re still having problems uploading a signature image, try uploading the image using an incognito window:

  • In Chrome, open a new incognito window. Detailed instructions
  • Log into your Google account.
  • Go to your Gmail settings and upload a signature image as you normally would. Detailed instructions
  • Close incognito mode. Detailed instructions Upload the image with a different browser

If you can’t upload an image with the other solutions in this section, try uploading the image using a different browser.

Signature image formatting or display issues

Signature images can have formatting or display issues. Examples include when an image:

  • Appears as a question mark or a broken image icon
  • Is the wrong size
  • Can’t be formatted Try the solutions in this section to fix issues with signature image formatting.

Delete then re-upload the signature image

Delete your signature image, and upload it again. For detailed instructions, go to Create a Gmail signature.

Use a different upload method

There are 3 ways to add an image to your signature:

  • Web Address (URL)–Enter the URL of an image that is publicly available on the web
  • My Drive–Browse and select a public image from your Google Drive
  • Upload–Upload an image file from your device, such as a phone, tablet, or computer. If you can’t add an image to your signature with one of the methods, try the other 2 methods.

Use a signature image in the recommended size

We recommend a signature image that’s 70–100 pixels high by 300–400 pixels wide. The maximum size for email signature images is 100 pixels high by 1000 pixels wide.

Try these options to resize the image:

  • Resize the image on a computer or mobile device before you upload it to your signature.
  • After you upload the image to your signature, select the image in the signature editor. Then, select a size option: Small, Medium, Large, or Original size.
  • Add the image to a Google Doc and resize the image in the Doc. Then, copy the image and paste it into your signature.

Turn Google Chat notifications on or off

Turn Google Chat notifications on or off

Notifications appear on the devices you used most recently. If you’re not active in Chat, notifications appear on all devices signed in to your Google Account.

By default, you receive notifications when:

  • Someone @ mentions you
  • Someone reacts or responds to your message If you mute a specific conversation or set your Chat status to “Do not disturb,” you won’t receive notifications.

In this article, learn how to:

  • Turn notifications on or off.

  • Customize notifications for specific conversations & spaces.

  • Customize notification sounds.

  • Get notifications in the Chat mobile app.

  • Update device or browser notification settings for Chat on a computer. Tips:

  • If email notifications are on, you get email reminders for Chat messages you haven’t read for more than 12 hours.

  • If you have multiple Google Accounts, you can set different notification settings for each account.

  • Some Google Chat apps can ignore your “Do Not Disturb” status or notification settings, to send updates, including:

    • @notify messages: These messages are for critical or time-sensitive information. They work like @all messages to get immediate attention and ignore your “Do Not Disturb” status, muted conversations, or notification settings.
    • @silent messages: These messages are for low-priority updates. They minimize disruption by working like system messages.
Google Chat: Manage your settings
Turn Google Chat notifications on or off

Turn on notifications

Turn on notifications in Google Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • To turn on notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” check the box next to “Allow chat notifications.” Tips:

  • If you don’t get Google Chat notifications after you turn it on, allow Google Chat notifications in your operating system and browser.

  • To turn email notifications for unread messages on or off, under “Email notifications,” select Only @mentions & direct messages or Off.

Manage combined notification permissions

Web users can grant browser notifications and idle detection permissions through a single flow. This occurs in two ways:

  • Enabled but blocked: If “Allow chat notifications” is enabled but the browser blocks notifications, a “Turn on” button appears. Click it to trigger permission dialogs.
  • Disabled toggle: If “Allow chat notifications” is disabled, turning on the toggle triggers permission dialogs.
Check if notifications are on
  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .
  • Under “Desktop notifications,” click Show an example.
  • If an example notification doesn’t appear:
    • Your notifications may be muted because of your availability status.
    • Turn on notifications for the device and browser you use with Google Chat.
Turn on notifications in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • To turn on notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” check the box next to “Allow chat notifications.”

Check if notifications are on

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings for Chat

  • Next to “Chat notifications settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” click Show an example.

  • If an example notification doesn’t appear:

    • Your notifications may be muted because of your availability status.
    • Turn on notifications for the device and browser you use with Gmail. Turn off notifications
Turn off notifications in Google Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • To turn off notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Allow chat notifications.” Tips:

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.” Learn how to change your availability status in Google Chat.

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn off Google Chat notifications in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings for Chat

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • To turn off notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Allow chat notifications.” Tips:

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.” Learn how to change your availability status in Google Chat.

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn Google Chat reaction notifications on or off

Turn on reaction notifications

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” check the box next to “Reaction notifications.” Tips:

  • For reaction notifications to work, turn on Allow chat notifications.

  • The existing notification settings apply to the reaction notifications of a conversation.

  • You can’t get reaction notifications in Announcement Spaces. Turn off reaction notifications

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Reaction notifications.”

    • This also turns off reaction notifications on mobile.
Customize Google Chat notifications for spaces & direct messages

Customize notifications for a space with in-line threading

By default, only threads you follow are bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list. To control how thread updates show in Chat, customize your notification settings.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Next to the space name, click More options Notifications.

  • Select an option for notifications:

    • All: Notifications for all new messages and replies to threads.
      • Tip: If you select “All,” it automatically follows all new threads for that space. To unfollow a thread, click Active Threads Following.
    • Main conversations: Notifications for all new main conversations, @mentions, and replies to threads you follow.
    • For you: Notifications for @mentions and replies to threads you follow.
    • None: No notifications, just an indicator for @mentions.

  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”

  • Click Save. Turn notifications on or off for a direct message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.

  • Next to the direct message or group DM, click More options Notifications.

    • For group DMs, you can select to get notifications for:
      • All: All new messages
      • For you: Only @mentions
      • None

  • Select All or None.

  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”

Customize Google Chat notification sounds

Customize notification sounds in Google Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Notifications sounds,” select the sound to use for notifications. Customize Google Chat notification sounds in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings for Chat

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • Under “Notifications sounds,” select the sound to use for notifications.

Grant idle detection permissions

Idle detection delivers notifications to your active device. Granting this permission helps reliably send notifications and pauses mobile alerts when you are active on desktop.

If you are idle on Gmail or Google Chat on your computer, notifications go to your mobile device. You are considered idle if you’re inactive for over 30 seconds, even if you still have a web browser open.

For Chrome users, you can adjust settings to receive chat notifications on mobile only when you’re inactive on Chrome.

Respond to the permission prompt

When you enable Chat notifications, a dialog may appear. This dialog asks you to “Pause mobile notifications when you are active on this device.” Click Continue to grant idle detection permission.

Adjust Chrome settings manually

If the permission dialog doesn’t appear, you can manually enable idle detection in your Chrome settings.

  • Go to chrome://settings/content/idleDetection.
  • Check the box for “Sites can ask to know when you’re actively using your device.”
  • Under “Customized behaviors,” add mail.google.com or chat.google.com to the allowed sites list.
  • To add a site, click Add.
Update device or browser notification settings

Update device notifications

Each computer operating system has different steps to turn on notifications. For more info, go to your operating system’s online help.

Some computer operating systems have settings that mute notifications. If you don’t get the notifications, make sure notifications aren’t muted.

Update browser notifications

To turn notifications on or off, you might need to update your browser notification settings. Learn how to allow Google Chat notifications.

Turn Google Chat notifications on or off

Turn on notifications

Turn on notifications in the Google Chat app

  • Open the Chat app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings . Go to Chat settings

  • Under “Notifications,” turn “Mobile notifications” on. Tip: If you don’t get notifications, make sure “Do not disturb” is off and notifications in your mobile device settings are on.

Turn on Google Chat notifications in the Gmail app
  • Open the Gmail app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  • Select your account.
  • Under “Notifications,” check the box next to “Chat notifications.” Tip: If you don’t get notifications, make sure “Do not disturb” is off and notifications in your mobile device settings are on.

Turn off notifications

Turn off notifications in the Google Chat app

  • Open the Chat app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings . Go to Chat settings

  • Under “Notifications,” turn “Mobile notifications” off. Tips:

  • If you still get notifications, you can turn off Google Chat app notifications in your mobile device settings.

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.”

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn off Google Chat notifications in the Gmail app

  • Open the Gmail app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .

  • Select your account.

  • Under “Notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Chat notifications.” Tips:

  • If you still get notifications, you can turn off Google Chat app notifications in your mobile device settings.

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.”

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn Google Chat reaction notifications on or off

Turn on reaction notifications

  • Open the Chat app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  • Under “Notifications,” turn on “Reaction notifications.” Tip: For reaction notifications to work, turn on Allow chat notifications.

Turn off reaction notifications

  • Open the Chat app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  • Under “Notifications,” turn off “Reaction notifications.”
    • This also turns off reaction notifications.
Customize Google Chat notifications for spaces & direct messages

Customize notifications for a space with in-line threading

By default, only threads you follow are bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list. To control how thread updates show in Chat, customize your notification settings.

  • On your Android phone or tablet, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • Select the Spaces tab at the bottom of the screen.
  • Tap and hold a space Notification settings.
  • Select an option for notifications:
    • All: Notifications for all new messages and replies to threads.
      • Tip: If you select “All,” it automatically follows all new threads for that space. To unfollow a thread, tap Active Threads Following.
    • Main conversations: Notifications for all new main conversations, @mentions, and replies to threads you follow.
    • For you: Notifications for @mentions and replies to threads you follow.
    • None: No notifications, just an indicator for @mentions.
  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.” Tip: When you follow a thread in a space, you’re notified with a blue dot whenever there’s activity in that thread unless that space is muted.

Turn notifications on or off for a specific direct message

  • On your Android phone or tablet, open the Chat app .
  • Tap and hold a direct message.
  • Tap Notification settings.
  • Select All or None.
  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”
Customize Google Chat notification sounds

Customize notification sounds in Google Chat app

  • Open the Chat app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings . Go to Chat settings

  • Under “Notifications,” tap Notification sound.

  • To update the notification sound or its volume, in the window that displays, tap Sound or See more for additional settings which include:

    • Toggle to allow notifications
    • Toggle to show notifications as pop-up
    • Toggle to Vibrate
    • Options for Lock screen
    • Toggle for App icon badges Tip: To turn off notification sounds, select None.

Customize Google Chat notification sounds in Gmail

  • Open the Gmail app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  • Tap General settings Manage notifications Chat and spaces Sound.
  • On the “Sound” screen, pick the notification sound you want to use.
  • On some Android phones, to save your notification sound, at the top right, tap Save.
Troubleshoot issues with Google Chat notifications

Prevent multiple notifications

To avoid duplicate mobile notifications from the Gmail and Chat apps, in your device’s settings, turn off Google Chat app notifications.

  • On your device, open the Settings app.
  • Tap Notifications App settings Chat.
    • If you don’t find “Chat,” update the list to show all apps:
      • At the top, tap the Down arrow All apps.
  • Turn “All Chat notifications” off. Tip: For more info, visit stop extra chat notifications.

Not getting notifications

If you don’t get notifications, visit I’m not getting Google Chat notifications.

Get notifications in the Google Chat mobile app

When the Google Chat mobile app is open, you get notifications in the app.

You won’t get notifications:

  • Online at chat.google.com
  • In the Chat desktop app
  • In Chat in Gmail When the Chat app is open, you get the message “You’re receiving Chat notifications here.” Learn more about the Chat standalone app.

Important: When iPhone or iPad users get messages from you, your profile picture could also appear on the notifications. Learn how to change your profile picture.

Turn Google Chat notifications on or off

Notifications appear on the devices you used most recently. If you’re not active in Chat, notifications appear on all devices signed in to your Google Account.

By default, you receive notifications when:

  • Someone @ mentions you
  • Someone reacts or responds to your message If you mute a specific conversation or set your Chat status to “Do not disturb,” you won’t receive notifications.

In this article, learn how to:

  • Turn notifications on or off.

  • Customize notifications for specific conversations & spaces.

  • Customize notification sounds.

  • Get notifications in the Chat mobile app.

  • Update device or browser notification settings for Chat on a computer. Tips:

  • If email notifications are on, you get email reminders for Chat messages you haven’t read for more than 12 hours.

  • If you have multiple Google Accounts, you can set different notification settings for each account.

  • Some Google Chat apps can ignore your “Do Not Disturb” status or notification settings, to send updates, including:

    • @notify messages: These messages are for critical or time-sensitive information. They work like @all messages to get immediate attention and ignore your “Do Not Disturb” status, muted conversations, or notification settings.
    • @silent messages: These messages are for low-priority updates. They minimize disruption by working like system messages.
Turn Google Chat notifications on or off

Turn on notifications

Turn on notifications in the Google Chat app
  • Open the Chat app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  • Under “Notifications,” turn on “Chat notifications.” Tip: If you don’t get notifications, make sure “Do not disturb” is off and notifications in your mobile device settings are on.
Turn on Google Chat notifications in the Gmail app
  • Open the Gmail app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  • Under “Notifications,” tap Chat notifications.
  • Turn on “Chat notifications.” Tip: If you don’t get notifications, make sure “Do not disturb” is off and notifications in your mobile device settings are on.

Turn off notifications

Turn off notifications in the Google Chat app

  • Open the Chat app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .

  • Under “Notifications,” turn off “Chat notifications.” Tips:

  • If you still get notifications, you can turn off Google Chat app notifications in your mobile device settings.

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.”

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn off Google Chat notifications in the Gmail app

  • Open the Gmail app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .

  • Under “Notifications,” tap Chat notifications.

  • Turn off “Chat notifications.” Tips:

  • If you still get notifications, you can turn off Google Chat app notifications in your mobile device settings.

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.”

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn Google Chat reaction notifications on or off

Turn on reaction notifications

  • Open the Chat app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  • Under “Notifications,” turn on “Reaction notifications.” Tip: For reaction notifications to work, turn on Allow chat notifications.

Turn off reaction notifications

  • Open the Chat app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  • Under “Notifications,” turn off “Reaction notifications.”
    • This also turns off reaction notifications.
Customize Google Chat notifications for spaces & direct messages

Customize notifications for a space with in-line threading

By default, only threads you follow are bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list. To control how thread updates show in Chat, customize your notification settings.

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • Tap and hold a space Notification settings.
  • Select an option for notifications:
    • All: Notifications for all new messages and replies to threads.
      • Tip: If you select “All,” it automatically follows all new threads for that space. To unfollow a thread, tap Active Threads Following.
    • Main conversations: Notifications for all new main conversations, @mentions, and replies to threads you follow.
    • For you: Notifications for @mentions and replies to threads you follow.
    • None: No notifications, just an indicator for @mentions.
  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, turn on Mute conversation. Tip: When you follow a thread in a space, you’re notified with a blue dot whenever there’s activity in that thread unless that space is muted.

Turn notifications on or off for a specific direct message

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app .
  • Tap and hold a direct message.
  • Tap Notification settings.
  • Select All or None.
  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, turn on Mute conversation.
Customize Google Chat notification sounds

Customize notification sounds in Google Chat app

  • Open the Chat app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .

  • Under “Notifications,” tap Notification sounds.

  • Select the notification sound you want to use.

  • To turn off notification sounds, tap None.

  • Tap Done. Customize Google Chat notification sounds in Gmail

  • Open the Gmail app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .

  • Under “Notifications,” tap Chat notifications Notification sounds.

  • Select the notification sound you want to use.

  • To turn off notification sounds, tap None.

  • Tap Done.

Troubleshoot issues with Google Chat notifications

Prevent multiple notifications

To avoid duplicate mobile notifications from the Gmail and Chat apps, in your device’s settings, turn off Google Chat app notifications.

  • On your device, open the Settings app.
  • Tap Notifications Chat.
  • Turn “Allow notifications” off. Tip: For more info, visit stop extra chat notifications.

Not getting notifications

If you don’t get notifications, visit I’m not getting Google Chat notifications.

Get notifications in the Google Chat mobile app

When the Google Chat mobile app is open, you get notifications in the app.

You won’t get notifications:

  • Online at chat.google.com
  • In the Chat desktop app
  • In Chat in Gmail When the Chat app is open, you get the message “You’re receiving Chat notifications here.” Learn more about the Chat standalone app.

Important: When iPhone or iPad users get messages from you, your profile picture could also appear on the notifications. Learn how to change your profile picture.

Update your Gmail app

Update your Gmail app

With the latest Gmail app, you’ll get:

  • Faster Gmail
  • Better security
  • New features, like email blocking and new formatting options Tip: If you use an older version of Gmail, the app may ask you to update before you can use it.

Update your Gmail app

What you can do with the latest Gmail app

After you update the app, you’ll find these changes to Gmail.

Secure your account

You get the latest security fixes and alerts, like:

  • Warnings when messages aren’t secure
  • Warnings about suspicious senders
  • Better authentication and sync Learn how to check security alerts in the latest Gmail app.

Change fonts, colors, and formats

Make messages easier to read with bold, colors, and other formats. Gmail shows your messages as if you sent them from a computer.

Learn how to change your formatting.

Block unwanted emails

If you get messages you don’t want, you can now block or unsubscribe from those messages.

Learn how to block senders.

Use Gmail features with other accounts

You can use Gmail features on other accounts you add to the Gmail app.

Learn how to get Gmail features for Yahoo, Outlook, and other non-Gmail accounts.

See all your inboxes

If you’ve added other accounts to the Gmail app, you can now check all your accounts in one inbox.

Learn how to check all your accounts.

Use Deep Research in Gemini in Workspace apps

Use Deep Research in Gemini in Workspace apps

Important: You can also use Deep Research in Gemini Apps, though certain features may vary from Gemini in Workspace apps. Learn how to use Deep Research in Gemini Apps.

You can conduct in-depth and real-time research on most subjects with Deep Research in Gemini in Workspace. You can change or add other sources, like your personal Gmail or Drive, for your research.

You can use Deep Research for Gemini in:

  • Chat
  • Docs
  • Drive
  • Gmail
  • Sheets
  • Slides
What you need

Availability of Deep Research features may vary based on your account type and specific Workspace app.

Chat

  • For personal Google Accounts:
    • You need access to Google Workspace Experiments, which is a trusted tester program to try new AI features. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace Experiments.
  • For work or school accounts:
    • You need access to Gemini Beta. Your administrator controls access to Gemini Beta. If you can’t find this feature, your administrator may not have Beta features enabled for your organization. Docs, Drive, Gmail, Sheets & Slides
  • For personal Google Accounts:
    • You need an eligible Google AI plan:
      • Google AI Plus
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra
    • You can also access Deep Research if your account is enrolled in Google Workspace Experiments, which is a trusted tester program to try new AI features. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace Experiments.
  • For work or school accounts: You need an eligible Google Workspace plan. Learn more about Gemini features and plans.
Start a Deep Research report

Start a Deep Research report in Chat

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .

    • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.

  • At the bottom, in the text box, enter a question or prompt that explains what you want to research. For example:

    • “Use Deep Research to examine current renewable energy trends and compare them with my project drafts in Drive.”
    • “Use Deep Research to recommend restaurants, attractions, and activities for my upcoming 7-day trip to Oslo, Norway.”

  • Click Send message . Start a Deep Research report in Docs, Drive, Gmail, Sheets, or Slides

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Gmail or Docs.

  • On the right, click Ask Gemini .

  • At the bottom, click Tools Deep Research.

  • In the text box, enter a question or prompt that explains what you want to research. For example:

    • “Research current renewable energy trends and compare them with my project drafts in Drive.”
    • “Find recommended restaurants, attractions, and activities for my upcoming 7-day trip to Oslo, Norway.”

  • Click Submit .

Set up the Deep Report report

Step 1: Add sources & review your research plan

After you submit your prompt, you can choose sources to help inform your research.

  • In the sources card, select one or more options:

    • Drive: Analyze files and folders in your Google Drive.
    • Gmail: Include info from your emails.
    • Chat: Include info from your chat messages.
    • Web: Search the public web for the latest info.

  • Optional for Docs, Drive, Gmail, Sheets, and Slides: To choose specific sources for your research, click Add sources and select files from your Drive.

  • Click Next.

    • Gemini creates a research plan for your topic.
    • To update the research plan before you create a report, click Customize.

  • Click Start research. Step 2: Track your research

  • While you work, Gemini researches your topic based on the plan.

  • It can take some time to generate your report since Gemini analyzes many sources.

  • You can close Gemini, start a new chat, or switch to a different Workspace document. The research task continues to run in the background.

  • When the research is complete:

    • Gemini generates the report in a Google Doc.
    • You get an email about your plan’s completion. Step 3: Open your report

  • In your conversation with Gemini, click Open Doc.

    • A new Google Doc opens in a new tab.
    • It includes the findings, citations, and an organized summary of the data found.
    • The report automatically saves to your Drive.

  • In the document, ask Gemini follow-up questions about the report.

    • You can also ask Gemini to refine specific sections.
Find your Deep Research reports

Find your Deep Research reports in Chat

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
    • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • Under “Recent,” select your research conversation.
    • To find more conversations, click Show more. Find your Deep Research reports in Docs, Drive, Gmail, Sheets, or Slides
  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Gmail or Docs.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left, click More options .
  • Under “History,” find your research conversation.
    • To find more conversations, click View all. Tips:
  • Your conversations are organized by date, with the most recent at the top.
  • You can also find your research reports at drive.google.com.
Related resources

  • Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet & Vids protects your data

Use Gmail on your watch

Use Gmail on your watch

From the Gmail app on your watch, you can:

  • Check your inbox

  • Read emails

  • Archive emails

  • Delete emails

  • Star emails

  • Mark emails as read or unread

  • Reply or reply all to emails

  • React to messages with emoji Some Gmail features aren’t supported on your watch:

  • Compose an email

  • View images or links in the email

  • View HTML emails

  • Open and download attachments

  • Search for emails

  • Check your spam folder

Get Gmail

Learn how to get the Gmail app on your watch.

Sign in to Gmail

Important: You can only add personal @gmail.com accounts to Gmail on Wear OS. Work and school accounts aren’t supported.

  • If you have one account on your watch, Gmail signs in automatically to that Google Account.
  • If you have more than one account on your watch, Gmail asks you to select the account you want active.
  • To switch the active Gmail account:
    • On your watch, open the Gmail app .
    • Tap Menu .
    • Tap your email address.
    • Select the email address you want to switch to Switch. Tip: Tiles or widgets and complications use the account that’s active in the Gmail app.
Check Gmail notifications on your watch
  • Gmail notifications that appear on your phone also appear on your watch.
  • Only email notifications sent to the active Gmail account can be opened in the app.
  • Gmail notifications may be disabled on some Wear OS watches. To enable them, go to the watch’s settings.
  • Learn how to fix issues with notifications on your watch.
Add Gmail complications

Important: Some of these steps may differ based on your Wear OS watch.

To find the number of new emails available on your watch face, add a complication. This number includes new emails that arrived in your inbox after you last opened it.

  • On your watch face, touch and hold the screen.
  • Tap Edit .
  • Swipe to the complication edit screen.
  • Tap the complication you want to change.
Add Gmail tiles or widgets

Important: Some of these steps may differ based on your Wear OS watch.

Your latest 2 emails display in the tile or widget. At the bottom, you can find the number of new emails available. Learn how to add tiles or widgets.

  • On your watch face, swipe left or right to go to a tile or widget.
  • Touch and hold a tile or widget.
  • At the bottom, tap Add .
  • Under “Add to carousel,” select the Gmail tile or widget.
Manage your inbox

Important: Your inbox layout is based on your current Gmail settings. To change your inbox layout, update your Gmail settings.

To focus on your most important emails, filter out unimportant emails from the primary inbox.

  • On your watch, open the Gmail app .
  • Find an email that you want to manage.
  • Select an option.
    • Star: At the bottom right of the email, tap the Star .
    • Archive: Swipe from right to left, then tap Archive . To undo, tap Undo.
    • Delete: Swipe from right to left, then tap Delete . To undo, tap Undo. Tip: To find your organized emails, at the top left of your inbox, tap Menu .
Check your emails
  • On your watch, open the Gmail app .
  • Tap an email.
  • Select an option.
    • Archive : When you archive an email, you move emails out of your inbox. Archived emails come back to your inbox when someone replies to them.
    • Delete : When you delete an email, you move emails to the trash. Deleted emails stay in your trash for 30 days. After that time, they’re permanently deleted from your account and can’t be recovered.
    • Star : When you star emails in Gmail, you mark them as important. Mark emails as important to help remind you to find them later.
    • Mark as unread: If you want to remember to read an email later, you can mark it as unread.
    • Open on phone: If you want to view an email on a larger screen or perform an action that isn’t supported, you can open it on your phone.
    • Reply or Reply all: You can reply to the sender or everyone who received the email with an emoji, voice dictation, or text response.
      • Emoji: To open the emoji menu, touch and hold a message.
        • If someone already replied with an emoji, under the message, you can tap the same emoji to reply.
      • Voice dictation: To create a voice dictated reply, tap the Microphone .
      • Text response: To type a text response, tap the Keyboard .

  • Change your Gmail inbox layout
  • Reply to emails with emoji reactions

Use Google Chat in Gmail

Use Google Chat in Gmail

To manage your communication, stay connected, and collaborate in one place, add Google Chat to your Gmail inbox. If you use a work or school account, your organization determines if this option is available.

Important: Your child can use Chat in the Gmail app, or in the web version of Gmail, even if the Chat app is blocked. Learn how to manage your child’s Google Account.

Turn Chat on or off in Gmail
  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • Go to Gmail settings
  • At the top, click Chat and Meet.
  • Next to “Chat,” to turn Chat on or off in Gmail, select Google Chat or Off.
  • Click Save Changes.
How is Chat in Gmail different from Chat?

You get the same features in Chat and Chat in Gmail, but the integrated Gmail experience provides a central location to communicate with friends, family, or coworkers between emails.

  • Chat: Use when you prefer a dedicated chat experience and don’t mind switching between different apps.
  • Gmail: Use when you like to multi-task and prefer to get all of your communications in one place. Learn more about the new integrated Gmail layout. Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad

Use hosted S/MIME to keep Gmail messages more secure

Use hosted S/MIME to keep Gmail messages more secure

If you’re using a work account and the option has been turned on by your organization, you can keep your email messages more secure by using Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME).

To use S/MIME, you need a S/MIME certificate uploaded to your account. Your Administrator may provide a certificate for you, or you may have to upload a Public-Key Cryptography Standards (PKCS) #12 certificate to Gmail through the Gmail settings. The certificate can be used to sign outgoing messages during transport. Other senders can use the public key to send you encrypted messages.

Manage account certificates

The next section, describes how to generate a PKCS #12 certificate file, sometimes called a “private certificate.” PKCS #12 is a bundle that includes your certificate and your private key. The certificate has your public key and email address, and it should be signed by a Certificate Authority (CA).

To use S/MIME, you or your system administrator have to upload the PKCS #12 file to your Gmail account. This section explains how you can upload certificates from the Gmail settings.

When you receive a message that is digitally signed with S/MIME, Gmail automatically associates the public key with a contact. You don’t have to manually create a contact.

When you send a message, if there is a public key associated with the recipient in your contacts, Gmail automatically encrypts the message.

If you add more than one PKCS #12 certificate to your Gmail account, you need to set a default S/MIME certificate that Gmail will use to sign outgoing messages.

Why would you upload more than one certificate?

One reason you might want to upload more than one certificate is if your current certificate is about to expire and you want to add a new one. You’d upload the new certificate and keep the previous one on your Gmail account. Gmail uses all the uploaded certificates to decrypt incoming messages. So if people who only have your previous public key send you encrypted emails, Gmail will be able to decrypt them.

Upload a certificate

To upload a PKCS #12 file with your certificate and private key:

  • In Gmail, click Settings See all settings.
  • At the top, click the Accounts and Import or Accounts tab.
  • In the Send mail as section, click edit info next to your work account.
  • Click Upload a personal certificate. A window opens showing the files available on your system.
  • You might not have this option if your organization doesn’t allow it.
  • Select the certificate file.
  • Enter the password and click Add Certificate.
Change the default certificate
  • In the Edit email address window, locate the entry for the certificate.
  • Select the certificate to make it the default.
Remove a certificate

You can remove certificates that are expired, revoked, or otherwise no longer required.

  • In the Edit email address window, locate the entry for the certificate and click remove.
  • Click Remove Certificate.
How do I get certificates?

Your certificate should be signed by a Certificate Authority (CA).

There are 2 primary ways to get a PKCS #12 certificate file:

  • Your system administrator will generate it for you. In this case, they can either directly upload it to Gmail or they can give it to you and you’ll upload it using the S/MIME Settings in Gmail.

  • You can use a CA to generate a PKCS #12 file. This section explains what you need to do to create the PKCS #12 file that you’ll upload using the S/MIME Settings in Gmail. To generate a PKCS #12 file that includes your certificate and your private key:

  • First, go to the web site of a trusted CA to request a certificate. Certificates have to adhere to certain public-key cryptography standards to be trusted. When you request a certificate, your browser will generate a public/private key pair and will send the public key to the CA

  • The CA will generate a signed certificate containing your public key and your email address. Most CAs will send you a link with the certificate file to download. This file often has a .pem or .crt extension.

  • Generate the PKCS #12 file on the same machine and browser that you used to request the certificate. The steps are different for each platform: Generate a PKCS #12 file on Macintosh OS/X with Chrome 55

  • Open the certificate file provided by your CA by double clicking on the file. This opens the Keychain Access utility of the MAC OS. Add the certificate to the keychain ‘login’.

  • Go to chrome://settings.

  • At the bottom, click Show advanced settings.

  • Scroll to the HTTPS/SSL section and click Manage certificates.

  • The Keychain Access utility will open. Chrome uses it to manage digital certificate. Under ‘Keychains’ on the left, select ‘Login’ and click ‘My Certificates’ in the ‘Category’ column. Then select the certificate that was provided by your CA.

  • On the top menu, click File > Export Items.

  • Select the file format ‘Personal Information Exchange (.p12)’, enter a name for the file and click the Save button.

  • A window appears, prompting you to enter a password to protect the exported file. Certificates for Chrome 51 on Ubuntu

  • Go to chrome://settings.

  • At the bottom, click Show advanced settings.

  • Scroll to the HTTPS/SSL section and click Manage certificates.

  • Click the Import button. Select the certificate file provided by your CA. Click open. The certificate will be added to Chrome.

  • The window will close. Scroll to the HTTPS/SSL section again and click Manage certificates.

  • Click the certificate to select it. Click Export. Select a name and a password for the PKCS #12 file that will contain both your certificate and private key. Certificates for Internet Explorer 11 on Windows 10

  • The CA-provided certificate is saved on the browser’s certificate store.

  • Open Internet Explorer.

  • From the menu bar, click Tools or click Settings at the top.

  • From the drop-down menu, select Internet options.

  • On the Content tab, select Certificates.

  • Click on a certificate to select it.

  • Click Export to open the export wizard and then click Next.

  • Select Yes, export the private key.

  • Note: If this option doesn’t appear, verify that you selected the correct certificate in the previous steps.

  • Click Next.

  • Select .pfx and click Next.

  • Select the Password box, enter and confirm your password, and click Next.

  • Enter the name of the file and click Next.

  • Review settings and click Finish. Note: Be sure to enter a password when you generate the PKCS #12 file because it will contain your private key. Do not use your Gmail password. You’ll need to enter this password when you upload the file to the Gmail settings.

Can I generate a PKCS #12 file on Chrome OS?

No, Generating a PKCS #12 file on Chrome OS is not currently supported.

Use integrations with Gemini in Workspace

Use integrations with Gemini in Workspace

With Gemini in Google Workspace, you can connect to and retrieve information from third-party services like Asana and Mailchimp. These are known as integrations.

You can use an integration with Gemini in:

  • Chat

  • Docs

  • Drive

  • Gmail

  • Sheets

  • Slides Important: For specific steps on connecting integrations in Sheets or Chat:

  • Learn more about integrations in Chat

  • Learn more about integrations in Sheets For all other Workspace apps, learn how to use an integration.

What you need
  • A supported personal, work, or school account:
    • For personal accounts, you need:
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra
    • For work or school accounts, you need:
      • Business Standard
      • Business Plus
      • Enterprise Standard
      • Enterprise Plus
      • Enterprise Essentials
      • Enterprise Essential Plus
      • Google AI Pro for Education
  • A required third-party subscription: In addition to any required Google AI plans or Google Workspace editions, some integrations require a subscription to use with Gemini in Workspace. Check the page for the integration when you install it for details.
  • Administrator permission for work or school accounts: Your account’s Google Workspace administrator enables the ability to connect integrations to Gemini in Workspace. If you can’t use an integration, ask your administrator to allow it or connect it for you.
Connect an integration
  • On your computer, go to the Google Workspace Marketplace integrations page.
    • This page provides a pre-filtered view of integrations that work with Gemini in Workspace.
  • Select the integration you want to connect to Gemini in Workspace.
  • Click Connect.
  • To grant the integration access to your Google Account data and complete the connection, follow the on-screen instructions.
    • A third-party helper app might be required. To check if a helper app is needed, review the app’s details page in the Workspace Marketplace. Any requirements are listed in the “Overview” section.
Explore available integrations

Important: Integrations currently only support read actions, such as searching for or finding information. You can’t use an integration to make changes to third-party apps.

Integration

Description

Asana

Find specific projects, tasks, or subtasks within your workspace. You can also check the current status of assigned work.

Atlassian-Rovo (Jira, Confluence)

Track down specific Jira issues and project details. Locate relevant documentation across your Confluence pages.

HubSpot

Access your CRM data to find specific contacts or companies. View the details of active deals directly in your prompt.

Mailchimp

Retrieve details about your email campaigns and audience lists. Pull up recent subscriber reports to review performance.

Monday.com

Query your boards for updates on ongoing projects. Quickly locate individual tasks and their details.

QuickBooks

Retrieve financial records like customer invoices and logged expenses. Look up specific billing details directly from Workspace.

Salesforce

Look up customer contacts and associated companies. Review active leads and pipeline opportunities.

Use an integration

  • On your computer, open a supported Gemini in Workspace app.

  • In your Workspace app, find and open Ask Gemini .

  • In the text box at the bottom, enter @.

  • Select the integration you want to use.

  • Enter your prompt with instructions or questions for Gemini.

  • Press Enter. Examples:

  • “What @Asana issues assigned to me are due today?”

  • “What’s the current pipeline looking like for my open opportunities in @Salesforce right now?”

Delete a connection to an integration

Through your Google Account security settings, you can review and delete connections to third-party integration. When you delete a connection, data sharing between Gemini in Workspace and that integration stops.

To delete an integration:

  • On your computer, open a browser.

  • In your browser, go to Google Account security settings.

  • Find the “Your connections to third-party app & services” card.

  • Click See all connections.

  • Select the app name you want to disconnect.

  • Click Delete all connections you have with [name of app].

  • In the pop-up window, click Confirm. Tip: To manage administrator controls:

  • Learn more about workplace integration steps.

  • Learn how to manage the Marketplace app allowlist.

Use Suggested Replies in Gmail

Use Suggested Replies in Gmail

If you’re short on time or need to find the right words, Gemini in Gmail can review an email that you receive and suggest a relevant response. With Suggested Replies, you get a personalized message that matches the tone and style of your past written emails.

What you need

Important: Even if you meet the requirements, a suggested reply may not always be available.

To get a suggested reply, make sure:

  • Workspace smart features are on in your Gmail settings. Learn more about smart features.
  • Your Google Account language is set to English. Learn how to change your language.
Select a suggested reply
  • On your computer, go to Gmail.
  • Open an email.
  • At the bottom of the email, click the suggested reply.
    • Before you send a response, you can edit it.
  • Click Send.
Learn how Gmail personalizes Suggested Replies

Important:

  • Suggested Replies with personalization are available in English only.
  • To get personalized responses, you need an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Personalization is not available for personal Google Accounts without a Google AI plan. Learn about Gemini features and plans. To improve your response, Suggested Replies use details from your emails, such as flight times, soccer schedules, or hotel booking codes. Gmail drafts a personalized response with relevant details and matches your tone and style.

Tip: To find the emails Gemini uses, select Sources above a suggestion. You can’t edit the list of sources.

Give feedback about a suggested reply

Google Workspace with Gemini is constantly learning and may not be able to support your request. Because feedback may be human readable, please do not submit data that contains personal, confidential, or sensitive information.

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can submit feedback.

  • At the top of the suggested reply, click Send feedback .

  • Write your feedback.

  • Click Submit. Important:

  • To send feedback with screenshots, at the top right, click Help Send feedback to Google. Learn more about sending feedback in Gmail.

  • To report a legal issue, create a request.

Learn about Gemini feature suggestions
  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.
  • Don’t rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial or other professional advice.
  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information.
Related resources
  • Get started with Google Workspace with Gemini
  • Draft emails with Gemini in Gmail
  • Collaborate with Gemini in Gmail Computer AndroidiPhone & iPad

Learn about Workspace Experiments feature suggestions
  • Workspace Experiments feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.

  • Your Workspace Experiments Data may also be read, rated, annotated, and reviewed by human reviewers. Importantly, where Google uses Google-selected input (as described in the Privacy Notice) to generate output, Google will aggregate and/or pseudonymize that content and resulting output before it is viewed by human reviewers, unless it is specifically provided as part of your feedback to Google.
How Workspace Experiments data in Gmail is collected

When you select a suggested reply in Gmail, Google uses and stores the following data:

  • The email thread
  • The suggested reply you select
  • Your feedback on a suggested reply To understand how this data is used, review the Google Workspace Experiments Privacy Notice and Terms for Personal Accounts.

Use summary cards in Gmail

Use summary cards in Gmail

Summary cards provide important information from your email about:

  • Order tracking
  • Events
  • Travel
  • Bills
  • Promotions
Availability

Summary cards are available in Gmail for the web and in the app for Android, iPhone, and iPad.

How summary cards work

To show you the important information from your email, summary cards will display at the top of your inbox.

For example, you can:

  • Find an order delivery status and bookings.
  • Invite others to your events on Google Calendar.
  • Create a task to remind you about an upcoming bill. Summary cards are generated based on the information from your email. To check the emails that the summary card is based on, click Based on [x] email. If you notice anything incorrect about the summary card, click feedback icons or below the card.
Show or hide summary cards in Gmail

Important: By default, smart features are turned off if you’re in:

  • The European Economic Area

  • Japan

  • Switzerland

  • United Kingdom To show summary cards:

  • Go to Gmail settings.

  • Turn on:

    • Smart features for Gmail, Chat, and Meet
    • Conversation view To hide summary cards, turn off smart features for Gmail, Chat, and Meet.

Tips:

  • If you don’t get a summary card, or the summary card has limited information, there may not be enough details in the email. To request another provider for summary cards, you can submit feedback in Gmail.
  • If you turn on live package tracking, you can get the latest information about your order from the carrier on the estimated delivery date and time. Learn about package tracking in Gmail.
  • If you don’t get a reminder for an upcoming bill, check if you have the right settings in your preferred task management app. Learn more about notifications for tasks.

Use the latest version of Gmail in your browser

Use the latest version of Gmail in your browser

If your browser is supported, Gmail automatically opens to the most recent version with the latest features and security updates. Learn how to use supported browsers for Gmail.

Tip: You can also use the latest version of Gmail with screen readers.

Learn how to fix issues when Gmail doesn’t load

If Gmail won’t load, check your browser, internet connection, or device for issues.

Check your browser

  • Use a supported browser.

    • Most browsers support Gmail. If you have trouble using your browser with Gmail:
      • Update your browser version to the latest version.
      • Try another browser.

  • Check your browser extensions or applications.

    • Some extensions or add-ons on your browser or applications on your computer may cause Gmail to not work.
    • Turn off extensions and uninstall applications one by one. Then, open Gmail again to check if that solves the problem.
    • If available, try using your browser’s incognito or private browsing mode.

  • Clear your browser’s cache and cookies, then open Gmail again. Check your internet connection

  • Restart your device.

  • Turn off your Wi-Fi or mobile data connection, then turn it back on again.

    • Tip: For Wi-Fi, if Gmail still does not load, restart your router. Check your router’s manual for instructions on how to restart it.

  • Connect to another network. If you still have connectivity issues after you complete these steps, contact your service provider or your Wi-FI network host.

Try another device

Gmail may not load in browsers on older devices. Try using another device to check if Gmail loads correctly.

If you still can’t get Gmail to load in your browser, you can:
  • Use the Gmail app for Android, iPhone, or iPad.
  • Download Gmail for Android Download Gmail for iPhone or iPad
  • Use Gmail with another email client.
    • You can use Gmail with other email clients that support IMAP and POP, such as Outlook or Apple Mail.
      • Learn how to read Gmail messages using IMAP.
      • Learn how to read Gmail messages using POP.
